source.text: Πέτρος δὲ καὶ Ἰωάννης ἀνέβαινον εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἐπὶ τὴν ὥραν τῆς προσευχῆς τὴν ἐνάτην, καί τις ἀνὴρ χωλὸς ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτοῦ ὑπάρχων ἐβαστάζετο, ὃν ἐτίθουν καθ’ ἡμέραν πρὸς τὴν θύραν τοῦ ἱεροῦ τὴν λεγομένην Ὡραίαν τοῦ αἰτεῖν ἐλεημοσύνην παρὰ τῶν εἰσπορευομένων εἰς τὸ ἱερόν, ὃς ἰδὼν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην μέλλοντας εἰσιέναι εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἠρώτα ἐλεημοσύνην λαβεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Peter now and John were going up into the temple at the hour of the prayer the ninth. \v 2 And a certain man lame from womb of mother of him being was being carried, whom they were placing daily at the gate of the temple the called Beautiful to ask alms from those going into the temple, \v 3 who having seen Peter and John about to go into the temple was asking alms to receive.

en.L: Now Peter and John were going up into the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth [hour]. \v 2 And a certain man who was lame from his mother's womb was being carried, whom they would put every day at the gate of the temple called Beautiful, to ask for alms from those going into the temple. \v 3 Seeing Peter and John about to go into the temple, he began asking to receive alms.
en.B: Peter and John were on their way up to the temple for the afternoon prayer at three o'clock. \v 2 Some people were carrying there a man who had been lame since birth. Every day they set him down by the temple gate known as the Beautiful Gate, so that he could beg from the people going in. \v 3 When he saw Peter and John about to enter the temple, he begged them for a gift.
en.R: One afternoon at three o'clock, Peter and John were going to the temple. It was the time when people went there to pray. \v 2 A man who had never been able to walk was being carried to the temple. Every day people put him beside one of the temple gates, the one called the Beautiful Gate. There he begged for money from the people going into the temple. \v 3 He saw Peter and John about to go in, and he asked them for money.

fr.L: Or Pierre et Jean montaient au temple à l’heure de la prière, la neuvième. \v 2 Et un homme, boiteux dès le ventre de sa mère, était porté ; on le plaçait chaque jour à la porte du temple qu’on nomme la Belle, pour demander l’aumône aux gens qui entraient dans le temple. \v 3 Voyant Pierre et Jean qui allaient entrer dans le temple, il leur demandait à recevoir une aumône.
fr.B: Pierre et Jean montaient au temple pour la prière de l’après-midi, à quinze heures. \v 2 Des gens y portaient un homme infirme depuis sa naissance. Chaque jour, on l’installait près de la porte du temple qu’on appelle la Belle Porte, pour qu’il puisse mendier auprès de ceux qui entraient. \v 3 Quand il vit Pierre et Jean sur le point d’entrer dans le temple, il leur demanda un don.
fr.R: Un après-midi, à quinze heures, Pierre et Jean allaient au temple. C’était l’heure où les gens y allaient pour prier. \v 2 On portait vers le temple un homme qui n’avait jamais pu marcher. Chaque jour, des gens l’installaient près d’une des portes du temple, celle qu’on appelle la Belle Porte. Là, il demandait de l’argent aux gens qui entraient dans le temple. \v 3 Il a vu Pierre et Jean qui allaient entrer, et il leur a demandé de l’argent.

decisions.choice: the ninth hour: about three in the afternoon, a set time of prayer
decisions.reason: Hours were counted from sunrise. The afternoon sacrifice was offered at this hour, and people gathered to pray (Luke 1:10; Acts 10:30; compare Daniel 9:21).

decisions.choice: the gate called Beautiful: a temple gate not named elsewhere
decisions.reason: No other ancient writing uses this name. It is often taken to be the great bronze gate that led from the outer court into the Court of the Women, but that cannot be proved.

decisions.choice: to ask for alms: to beg for gifts given out of mercy
decisions.reason: The word means a gift of mercy to the poor. Giving it was a religious duty (Luke 11:41, 12:33), and a temple gate was a good place to beg.

decisions.choice: lame from his mother's womb: unable to walk from birth
decisions.reason: He was over forty years old (4:22), and had never walked.

decisions.choice: the afternoon prayer at three o'clock
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the clock time; Literal keeps the Greek count of hours.

decisions.choice: had never been able to walk
decisions.reason: Readable says what "lame" means.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R), as in chapters 1-2; imperfects for the ongoing scene
decisions.reason: As recorded at 1:1 for the whole book. The Greek imperfects of 3:1-3 (they were going up, he was being carried, he kept asking) stay imperfects at every level; the story's events take the passé simple at Literal and Balanced and the passé composé at Readable.

decisions.choice: "monter au temple" for going to the temple; "la cour du temple" (B, R) once inside (3:8)
decisions.reason: The term sheet names the courts at Balanced and Readable where the Greek means the temple area (2:46). For going up to it, "monter au temple" is the natural French and already means the whole complex; once the man walks in with them, the courts are named.

source.text: ἀτενίσας δὲ Πέτρος εἰς αὐτὸν σὺν τῷ Ἰωάννῃ εἶπεν· Βλέψον εἰς ἡμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: Having looked intently now Peter at him with John said, Look at us.

en.L: And Peter, looking intently at him, with John, said, "Look at us."
en.B: Peter, together with John, gazed straight at him and said, "Look at us."
en.R: Peter and John looked straight at him. Peter said, "Look at us!"

fr.L: Et Pierre, fixant les yeux sur lui, avec Jean, dit : « Regarde-nous. »
fr.B: Pierre, avec Jean, le regarda droit dans les yeux et dit : « Regarde-nous. »
fr.R: Pierre et Jean l’ont regardé bien en face. Pierre a dit : « Regarde-nous ! »

decisions.choice: looking intently: a steady, searching look
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 1:10 and 3:12. Peter's look meets the beggar's request.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἐπεῖχεν αὐτοῖς προσδοκῶν τι παρ’ αὐτῶν λαβεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: He and was giving attention to them, expecting something from them to receive.

en.L: And he gave attention to them, expecting to receive something from them.
en.B: He kept his eyes on them, hoping they would give him something.
en.R: So the man looked at them. He thought they were going to give him something.

fr.L: Et lui était attentif à eux, s’attendant à recevoir d’eux quelque chose.
fr.B: Il ne les quittait pas des yeux, espérant qu’ils lui donneraient quelque chose.
fr.R: Alors l’homme les a regardés. Il pensait qu’ils allaient lui donner quelque chose.

decisions.choice: gave attention: fixed his eyes and mind on them
decisions.reason: The verb means to hold one's attention on something. He expects a coin.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ Πέτρος· Ἀργύριον καὶ χρυσίον οὐχ ὑπάρχει μοι, ὃ δὲ ἔχω τοῦτό σοι δίδωμι· ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου περιπάτει.

records.literal_gloss: Said but Peter, Silver and gold not there is to me, what but I have this to you I give: in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene walk.

en.L: But Peter said, "Silver and gold I do not have, but what I have, this I give you: in the name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} the Nazarene, walk."
en.B: But Peter said, "I have no silver or gold, but I will give you what I do have. In the name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} of Nazareth, walk!"
en.R: But Peter said, "I do not have any money. But I have something else, and I will give it to you. By the power of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} from Nazareth, walk!"

fr.L: Mais Pierre dit : « De l’argent et de l’or, je n’en ai pas ; mais ce que j’ai, cela je te le donne : au nom de Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} le Nazaréen, marche. »
fr.B: Mais Pierre dit : « Je n’ai pas d’argent, pas d’or non plus, mais ce que j’ai, je vais te le donner. Au nom de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, de Nazareth, marche ! »
fr.R: Mais Pierre a dit : « Je n’ai pas d’argent. Mais j’ai autre chose, et je vais te le donner. Par la puissance de Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, l’homme de Nazareth, marche ! »

decisions.choice: in the name of Jesus: by his authority and power
decisions.reason: Peter explains in 3:16 and 4:10 that Jesus's name healed the man. The name stands for the person himself.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "walk"
alternatives: many manuscripts read "get up and walk"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, have "get up and walk", perhaps from Luke 5:23. Others, some of them early, have only "walk". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: walk: start walking, and go on walking
decisions.reason: The present imperative suits an ongoing action: from now on, walk.

decisions.choice: silver and gold: money
decisions.reason: Silver and gold coins. The apostles had no money of their own to give (compare 2:44-45).

decisions.choice: by the power of
decisions.reason: Readable says what the name means here, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: καὶ πιάσας αὐτὸν τῆς δεξιᾶς χειρὸς ἤγειρεν αὐτόν· παραχρῆμα δὲ ἐστερεώθησαν αἱ βάσεις αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰ σφυδρά, καὶ ἐξαλλόμενος ἔστη καὶ περιεπάτει, καὶ εἰσῆλθεν σὺν αὐτοῖς εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν περιπατῶν καὶ ἁλλόμενος καὶ αἰνῶν τὸν θεόν.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken him by the right hand he raised up him; immediately and were made strong the feet of him and the ankles, \v 8 and leaping up he stood and was walking, and he entered with them into the temple, walking and leaping and praising the God.

en.L: And taking him by the right hand, he raised him up, and immediately his feet and ankles were made strong, \v 8 and leaping up he stood and began walking, and he entered with them into the temple, walking and leaping and praising God.
en.B: Peter took him by the right hand and lifted him up. At once the man's feet and ankles grew firm; \v 8 he sprang up, stood, and walked about. He went with them into the temple, walking and leaping and praising God.
en.R: Peter took hold of the man's right hand and helped him up. Right away the man's feet and ankles became strong. \v 8 He jumped up, stood on his feet, and started to walk. Then he went into the temple with Peter and John. He was walking and jumping and praising God.

fr.L: Et l’ayant saisi par la main droite, il le releva ; et à l’instant ses pieds et ses chevilles furent affermis, \v 8 et, bondissant, il se dressa et marchait, et il entra avec eux dans le temple, en marchant, en bondissant et en louant Dieu.
fr.B: Pierre le prit par la main droite et le releva. Aussitôt, les pieds et les chevilles de l’homme se raffermirent ; \v 8 il se leva d’un bond, se tint debout et fit quelques pas. Puis il entra avec eux dans la cour du temple, en marchant, en sautant et en louant Dieu.
fr.R: Pierre a pris la main droite de l’homme et l’a aidé à se lever. Tout de suite, les pieds et les chevilles de l’homme sont devenus solides. \v 8 Il a sauté sur ses pieds, il s’est tenu debout et il a commencé à marcher. Ensuite, il est entré dans la cour du temple avec Pierre et Jean. Il marchait, il sautait et il louait Dieu.

decisions.choice: leaping: the lame leap, as Isaiah foretold
decisions.reason: Isaiah 35:6 says that when God comes to save, "the lame will leap like a deer". Jesus pointed to the lame walking as a sign of his work (Luke 7:22).

decisions.choice: raised him up: the same verb used for raising the dead
decisions.reason: The verb means to lift or raise. Peter will say that God raised Jesus (3:15), using it again.

decisions.choice: feet and ankles
decisions.reason: The words are precise ones for the soles of the feet and the ankle bones.

decisions.choice: Peter; the man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people, since the pronouns change from one to the other.

source.text: καὶ εἶδεν πᾶς ὁ λαὸς αὐτὸν περιπατοῦντα καὶ αἰνοῦντα τὸν θεόν, ἐπεγίνωσκον δὲ αὐτὸν ὅτι οὗτος ἦν ὁ πρὸς τὴν ἐλεημοσύνην καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῇ Ὡραίᾳ Πύλῃ τοῦ ἱεροῦ, καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν θάμβους καὶ ἐκστάσεως ἐπὶ τῷ συμβεβηκότι αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And saw all the people him walking and praising the God, \v 10 they recognized and him that this was the [one] for the alms sitting at the Beautiful Gate of the temple, and they were filled with wonder and amazement at the having happened to him.

en.L: And all the people saw him walking and praising God, \v 10 and they recognized him, that he was the one who sat for alms at the Beautiful Gate of the temple, and they were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.
en.B: Everyone there saw him walking about and praising God. \v 10 They knew him as the man who used to sit begging at the temple's Beautiful Gate, and they were filled with awe and astonishment at what had happened to him.
en.R: All the people saw him walking and praising God. \v 10 They knew he was the man who always sat by the Beautiful Gate of the temple, begging for money. They were amazed and could not understand what had happened to him.

fr.L: Et tout le peuple le vit marchant et louant Dieu, \v 10 et ils le reconnaissaient : c’était lui qui était assis pour l’aumône à la Belle Porte du temple ; et ils furent remplis de stupeur et d’étonnement devant ce qui lui était arrivé.
fr.B: Tous ceux qui étaient là le virent marcher et louer Dieu. \v 10 Ils savaient bien que c’était l’homme qui mendiait, assis à la Belle Porte du temple, et ils furent saisis de crainte et de stupéfaction devant ce qui lui était arrivé.
fr.R: Tout le monde l’a vu marcher et louer Dieu. \v 10 Les gens savaient que c’était l’homme qui était toujours assis près de la Belle Porte du temple pour demander de l’argent. Ils étaient très étonnés et ne comprenaient pas ce qui lui était arrivé.

decisions.choice: they recognized him: the healing could not be doubted
decisions.reason: The man had been seen at the gate every day (3:2), so everyone could see that he had been healed (4:16).

decisions.choice: wonder and amazement: awe at something beyond explaining
decisions.reason: The second word can mean a trance (10:10), but here, as in Luke 5:26, it means being beside oneself with astonishment.

source.text: Κρατοῦντος δὲ αὐτοῦ τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τὸν Ἰωάννην συνέδραμεν πᾶς ὁ λαὸς πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἐπὶ τῇ στοᾷ τῇ καλουμένῃ Σολομῶντος ἔκθαμβοι.

records.literal_gloss: Holding now him Peter and John ran together all the people to them in the porch the called Solomon's, greatly amazed.

en.L: And while he was holding on to Peter and John, all the people ran together to them in the porch called Solomon's, utterly amazed.
en.B: As he clung to Peter and John, the whole crowd came running to them in what was called Solomon's Porch, completely astonished.
en.R: The man kept holding on to Peter and John. All the people were amazed, and they ran to them at Solomon's Porch, a covered walkway in the temple courts.

fr.L: Et comme il retenait Pierre et Jean, tout le peuple accourut vers eux au portique dit de Salomon, tout stupéfait.
fr.B: Comme il ne lâchait pas Pierre et Jean, toute la foule, stupéfaite, accourut vers eux sous la galerie qu’on appelait le portique de Salomon.
fr.R: L’homme tenait toujours Pierre et Jean. Tout le peuple était très étonné, et les gens ont couru vers eux au portique de Salomon, une galerie couverte dans les cours du temple.

decisions.choice: Solomon's Porch: a roofed colonnade on the east side of the temple's outer court
alternatives: a part of Solomon's own temple
decisions.reason: Jesus walked there in winter (John 10:23), and the believers met there (5:12). It carried Solomon's name, though Solomon's temple was long gone.

decisions.choice: holding on to Peter and John: he would not let go of them
decisions.reason: The verb means to hold fast.

decisions.choice: a covered walkway in the temple courts
decisions.reason: Readable says what the porch was.

source.text: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Πέτρος ἀπεκρίνατο πρὸς τὸν λαόν· Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται, τί θαυμάζετε ἐπὶ τούτῳ, ἢ ἡμῖν τί ἀτενίζετε ὡς ἰδίᾳ δυνάμει ἢ εὐσεβείᾳ πεποιηκόσιν τοῦ περιπατεῖν αὐτόν;

records.literal_gloss: Having seen but the Peter answered to the people, Men Israelites, why do you marvel at this, or at us why do you stare as by [our] own power or godliness having made to walk him?

en.L: And seeing [it], Peter answered the people, "Men, Israelites, why do you marvel at this, or why do you stare at us, as though by [our] own power or godliness we had made him walk?
en.B: When Peter saw this, he addressed the people: "{{gender:People|Men}} of Israel, why are you amazed at this? Why fix your eyes on us, as if it were our own power or piety that made this man walk?
en.R: When Peter saw this, he said to the people, "People of Israel, why are you surprised by this? Why are you staring at us? We did not make this man walk by our own power, or because we are so good.

fr.L: Voyant [cela], Pierre répondit au peuple : « Hommes, Israélites, pourquoi vous étonnez-vous de ceci, ou pourquoi fixez-vous les yeux sur nous, comme si c’était par notre propre puissance ou piété que nous l’avions fait marcher ?
fr.B: En voyant cela, Pierre s’adressa au peuple : « {{gender:Israélites|Hommes d’Israël}}, pourquoi cela vous étonne-t-il ? Pourquoi nous regarder fixement, comme si c’était notre propre puissance ou notre piété qui avait fait marcher cet homme ?
fr.R: Quand Pierre a vu cela, il a dit aux gens : « Peuple d’Israël, pourquoi êtes-vous surpris par ce qui arrive ? Pourquoi nous regardez-vous comme ça ? Ce n’est pas par notre propre puissance que nous avons fait marcher cet homme, ni parce que nous sommes si bons.

decisions.choice: answered: spoke in reply to what was happening
decisions.reason: No one has asked a question. "Answered" means he responded to the crowd and their amazement.

decisions.choice: men, Israelites: a formal address to the people
decisions.reason: As in 2:22; the whole crowd is likely meant.

decisions.choice: godliness: devotion to God, piety
decisions.reason: Peter denies that the healing was a reward for their own holiness or done by their own power.

decisions.choice: People of Israel, with "Men of Israel" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As at 2:22.

decisions.choice: a plain statement
alternatives: as though we had made him walk?
decisions.reason: Readable states what Peter's question implies.

decisions.choice: {{gender:Israélites|Hommes d’Israël}}
decisions.reason: As at 2:22: French "Israélites", in the plural, takes in the men and women of the crowd, and keeps the address in the plural as the Greek has it; "Hommes d’Israël" is the alternative. Literal keeps "Hommes, Israélites".

source.text: ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακώβ, ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν, ἐδόξασεν τὸν παῖδα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν, ὃν ὑμεῖς μὲν παρεδώκατε καὶ ἠρνήσασθε κατὰ πρόσωπον Πιλάτου, κρίναντος ἐκείνου ἀπολύειν·

records.literal_gloss: The God of Abraham and of Isaac and of Jacob, the God of the fathers of us, glorified the servant of him Jesus, whom you indeed handed over and denied before [the] face of Pilate, having decided that one to release.

en.L: The God of Abraham and of Isaac and of Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Jesus, whom you handed over and denied in [the] presence of Pilate, when that one had decided to release [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}].
en.B: The God of Abraham, of Isaac and of Jacob, the God of our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}, has glorified {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Jesus. You handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over and rejected {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} before Pilate, even when Pilate had judged that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} should be set free.
en.R: The God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the God our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} worshiped, has given glory to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Jesus. But you handed Jesus over to be killed. Pilate decided to let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} go, but you turned against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in front of Pilate.

fr.L: Le Dieu d’Abraham et d’Isaac et de Jacob, le Dieu de nos pères, a glorifié {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur Jésus, que vous, vous avez livré et renié en face de Pilate, alors que celui-ci avait décidé de [{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] relâcher.
fr.B: Le Dieu d’Abraham, d’Isaac et de Jacob, le Dieu de nos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}, a glorifié {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur Jésus. Vous, vous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avez livré et vous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avez rejeté devant Pilate, alors même que Pilate avait jugé qu’il fallait {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} relâcher.
fr.R: Le Dieu d’Abraham, d’Isaac et de Jacob, le Dieu que nos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} adoraient, a donné la gloire à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur Jésus. Mais vous, vous avez livré Jésus pour qu’on {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tue. Pilate avait décidé de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} laisser partir, mais vous vous êtes tournés contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} devant Pilate.

decisions.choice: the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob: God's name to Moses at the burning bush
decisions.reason: God named himself this way in Exodus 3:6 and 3:15. Peter speaks of the God of Israel's fathers, not a new god.

decisions.choice: has glorified his servant: the words of Isaiah 52:13
decisions.reason: In the Greek of Isaiah 52:13 God says his servant "will be lifted up and glorified". That servant suffers for others (Isaiah 53) and is raised high. Peter calls Jesus the servant again in 3:26 and 4:27.

decisions.choice: servant: the servant of God, as in Isaiah
decisions.reason: The word can mean child or servant. With the allusion to Isaiah, "servant" fits; it is the word used of David in 4:25.

decisions.choice: denied: refused, disowned
decisions.reason: To deny someone is to refuse to acknowledge them, as Peter himself denied Jesus (Luke 22:57).

decisions.choice: Pilate had decided to release him
decisions.reason: Luke tells three times that Pilate found him not guilty and wanted to release him (Luke 23:4, 23:14-16, 23:20-22).

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means forebears, men and women; Literal keeps the Greek word.

decisions.choice: to be killed
decisions.reason: Readable says what the handing over led to.

source.text: ὑμεῖς δὲ τὸν ἅγιον καὶ δίκαιον ἠρνήσασθε καὶ ᾐτήσασθε ἄνδρα φονέα χαρισθῆναι ὑμῖν, τὸν δὲ ἀρχηγὸν τῆς ζωῆς ἀπεκτείνατε, ὃν ὁ θεὸς ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν, οὗ ἡμεῖς μάρτυρές ἐσμεν.

records.literal_gloss: You but the Holy and Righteous [One] denied and asked a man a murderer to be granted to you, \v 15 the and Author of the life you killed, whom the God raised from [the] dead, of which we witnesses are.

en.L: But you denied the Holy and Righteous One and asked for a man [who was] a murderer to be granted to you, \v 15 and you killed the Author of life, whom God raised from [the] dead, of which we are witnesses.
en.B: You turned your backs on the Holy and Righteous One and asked to have a murderer granted to you as a favor, \v 15 and you killed the Author of life. God raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from the dead; we are witnesses to that.
en.R: Jesus was holy, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did what was right, but you rejected {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. You asked Pilate to set a murderer free instead. \v 15 You killed the one who gives life! But God brought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} back to life, and we saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. We are witnesses.

fr.L: Mais vous, vous avez renié le Saint et le Juste, et vous avez demandé qu’un homme meurtrier vous soit accordé, \v 15 et vous avez tué l’Auteur de la vie, que Dieu a ressuscité d’entre les morts, ce dont nous sommes témoins.
fr.B: Vous avez tourné le dos au Saint et au Juste, et vous avez réclamé qu’on vous accorde la libération d’un meurtrier, \v 15 et vous avez tué l’Auteur de la vie. Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a ressuscité d’entre les morts ; nous en sommes témoins.
fr.R: Jésus était saint, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} faisait ce qui est juste, mais vous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avez rejeté. Vous avez plutôt demandé à Pilate de libérer un assassin. \v 15 Vous avez tué celui qui donne la vie ! Mais Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a ramené à la vie, et nous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avons vu. Nous en sommes témoins.

decisions.choice: the Holy and Righteous One: titles of Jesus as God's servant
decisions.reason: Isaiah 53:11 calls the servant "the righteous one"; Acts uses the title again (7:52, 22:14). The centurion at the cross said, "Surely this man was righteous" (Luke 23:47).

decisions.choice: a murderer: Barabbas, set free in Jesus's place
decisions.reason: Luke 23:18-25 tells of Barabbas, jailed for rebellion and murder, released at the crowd's demand.

decisions.choice: the Author of life: the one from whom life comes, and who leads into it
decisions.reason: The word means a founder or originator, and also a leader who goes first. 5:31 and Hebrews 2:10, 12:2 use it of Jesus. Both senses fit; the contrast is plain either way: they killed the giver of life, and God raised him.

decisions.choice: of which: witnesses that God raised him
decisions.reason: As at 2:32.

decisions.choice: Jesus was holy, and he did what was right
decisions.reason: Readable turns the titles into plain statements.

decisions.choice: the one who gives life
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the main sense of the title, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: καὶ ἐπὶ τῇ πίστει τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ τοῦτον ὃν θεωρεῖτε καὶ οἴδατε ἐστερέωσεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἡ πίστις ἡ δι’ αὐτοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ τὴν ὁλοκληρίαν ταύτην ἀπέναντι πάντων ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And on the faith of the name of him, this [man] whom you see and know made strong the name of him, and the faith the through him gave to him the complete soundness this before all of you.

en.L: And on the basis of faith in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name, this man whom you see and know, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name has made strong; and the faith that [is] through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} has given him this complete health before all of you.
en.B: This man you see and know was made strong by the name of Jesus, through faith in that name. The faith that comes through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} has given the man perfect health here in front of you all.
en.R: This man was made strong by the name of Jesus, because of faith in that name. You see him and you know him. The faith that comes through Jesus has made him completely well, as you can all see.

fr.L: Et sur la base de la foi en {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom, cet homme que vous voyez et connaissez, {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom l’a affermi ; et la foi qui [vient] par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} lui a donné cette pleine santé devant vous tous.
fr.B: Cet homme que vous voyez et que vous connaissez, c’est le nom de Jésus qui l’a rendu fort, grâce à la foi en ce nom. La foi qui vient par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a rendu à cet homme une santé parfaite, ici, sous vos yeux à tous.
fr.R: C’est le nom de Jésus qui a rendu cet homme fort, grâce à la foi en ce nom. Vous le voyez et vous le connaissez. La foi qui vient par Jésus l’a complètement guéri, comme vous pouvez tous le voir.

decisions.choice: a crowded sentence: the name of Jesus, with faith in it, healed the man
alternatives: the man was healed by faith alone
decisions.reason: Peter repeats "his name" and "faith" to make one point: Jesus himself did it, not the apostles (3:12).

decisions.choice: whose faith: the apostles', the man's, or both
decisions.reason: The sentence does not say. The man had asked only for money (3:3), so Peter's faith may be meant; but the man walked when told.

decisions.choice: the faith that is through him: faith that Jesus himself gives and calls out
decisions.reason: "Through him" says that the faith too came from Jesus.

decisions.choice: complete health: soundness in every part
decisions.reason: The word means wholeness; Isaiah 1:6 uses it in the Greek Old Testament of a body with no sound spot.

decisions.choice: the name of Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since the pronoun stands far from his name.

source.text: Καὶ νῦν, ἀδελφοί, οἶδα ὅτι κατὰ ἄγνοιαν ἐπράξατε, ὥσπερ καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες ὑμῶν·

records.literal_gloss: And now, brothers, I know that in ignorance you acted, as also the rulers of you.

en.L: And now, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, I know that you acted in ignorance, as did also your rulers.
en.B: Now, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, I know you did not understand what you were doing, and neither did your rulers.
en.R: My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, I know that you and your leaders did not really know what you were doing.

fr.L: Et maintenant, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, je sais que vous avez agi par ignorance, comme aussi vos chefs.
fr.B: Maintenant, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, je sais que vous ne compreniez pas ce que vous faisiez, et vos chefs non plus.
fr.R: Mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, je sais que vous et vos chefs, vous ne saviez pas vraiment ce que vous faisiez.

decisions.choice: in ignorance: they did not know who Jesus was
decisions.reason: Jesus prayed, "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing" (Luke 23:34). The law made a way for sins done unknowingly to be forgiven (Numbers 15:22-31). Ignorance does not remove guilt, but it leaves room to repent (3:19).

decisions.choice: your rulers: the Jewish leaders, the council and chief priests
decisions.reason: The same leaders Luke names in Luke 23:13 and Acts 4:5-8.

decisions.choice: brothers: fellow Jews, men and women
decisions.reason: Peter now speaks to the crowd as his own people.

decisions.choice: brothers and sisters, with "brothers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word means the whole people here, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: ὁ δὲ θεὸς ἃ προκατήγγειλεν διὰ στόματος πάντων τῶν προφητῶν παθεῖν τὸν χριστὸν αὐτοῦ ἐπλήρωσεν οὕτως.

records.literal_gloss: The but God, what he announced beforehand through mouth of all the prophets, to suffer the Christ of him, he fulfilled thus.

en.L: But the things God announced beforehand by [the] mouth of all the prophets, that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} would suffer, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has fulfilled in this way.
en.B: Yet by these events God made come true what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said beforehand through all the prophets, that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} would suffer.
en.R: But God had said long ago through all the prophets that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} would suffer. And now God has made it happen, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said.

fr.L: Mais ce que Dieu avait annoncé d’avance par la bouche de tous les prophètes, que {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} {{christos:Christ|Messie}} souffrirait, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’a accompli ainsi.
fr.B: Pourtant, par ces événements, Dieu a accompli ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait annoncé d’avance par la bouche de tous les prophètes : que {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} {{christos:Christ|Messie}} souffrirait.
fr.R: Mais Dieu avait dit il y a longtemps, par tous les prophètes, que {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} {{christos:Christ|Messie}} souffrirait. Et maintenant, Dieu l’a fait arriver, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’avait dit.

decisions.choice: the suffering Messiah: foretold by the prophets
decisions.reason: The risen Jesus showed this from the Scriptures (Luke 24:25-27, 24:44-46). Isaiah 53 is the plainest example.

decisions.choice: all the prophets: the prophets as a whole
decisions.reason: A way of saying that the whole witness of the prophets points this way (3:24).

decisions.choice: suffer: including his death
decisions.reason: As at 1:3.

decisions.choice: his Christ, with "Messiah" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As everywhere.

source.text: μετανοήσατε οὖν καὶ ἐπιστρέψατε πρὸς τὸ ἐξαλειφθῆναι ὑμῶν τὰς ἁμαρτίας, ὅπως ἂν ἔλθωσιν καιροὶ ἀναψύξεως ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ κυρίου καὶ ἀποστείλῃ τὸν προκεχειρισμένον ὑμῖν χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν, ὃν δεῖ οὐρανὸν μὲν δέξασθαι ἄχρι χρόνων ἀποκαταστάσεως πάντων ὧν ἐλάλησεν ὁ θεὸς διὰ στόματος τῶν ἁγίων ἀπ’ αἰῶνος αὐτοῦ προφητῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Repent therefore and turn back for the to be wiped out of you the sins, \v 20 so that may come times of refreshing from presence of the Lord and he may send the [one] appointed beforehand for you Christ Jesus, \v 21 whom it is necessary heaven indeed to receive until times of restoration of all things, of which spoke the God through mouth of the holy from age of him prophets.

en.L: Repent therefore and turn back, so that your sins may be wiped out, \v 20 so that times of refreshing may come from [the] presence of the Lord, and [that] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may send the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} appointed beforehand for you, Jesus, \v 21 whom heaven must receive until [the] times of [the] restoration of all things, of which God spoke through [the] mouth of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy prophets from of old.
en.B: Repent, then, and turn around, so that your sins may be erased, \v 20 that seasons of relief may come from the presence of the Lord, and that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may send you Jesus, the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} appointed for you beforehand. \v 21 Jesus must be welcomed into heaven and remain there until the time when everything is set right again, as God told long ago by the mouth of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy prophets.
en.R: So turn away from your sins and come back to God. Then God will wipe out your sins. \v 20 Times will come when the Lord gives you rest and new strength. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will send Jesus to you, the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose for you. \v 21 But Jesus must stay in heaven until the time when God puts everything right again. God promised this long ago through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy prophets.

fr.L: Repentez-vous donc et revenez, afin que vos péchés soient effacés, \v 20 pour que des temps de rafraîchissement viennent de la présence du Seigneur, et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} envoie le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} désigné d’avance pour vous, Jésus, \v 21 que le ciel doit recevoir jusqu’aux temps de la restauration de toutes choses, dont Dieu a parlé par la bouche de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} saints prophètes depuis toujours.
fr.B: Repentez-vous donc et faites demi-tour, pour que vos péchés soient effacés, \v 20 que des temps de soulagement viennent de la présence du Seigneur, et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous envoie Jésus, le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a désigné d’avance pour vous. \v 21 Jésus doit être accueilli au ciel et y rester jusqu’au temps où tout sera remis en ordre, comme Dieu l’a annoncé depuis longtemps par la bouche de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} saints prophètes.
fr.R: Détournez-vous donc de vos péchés et revenez à Dieu. Alors Dieu effacera vos péchés. \v 20 Des temps viendront où le Seigneur vous donnera du repos et des forces nouvelles. Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous enverra Jésus, le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a choisi pour vous. \v 21 Mais Jésus doit rester au ciel jusqu’au moment où Dieu remettra tout en ordre. Dieu l’a promis il y a longtemps par {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} saints prophètes.

decisions.choice: turn back: return to God
decisions.reason: The prophets call Israel to turn back to God (Isaiah 55:7; Jeremiah 3:12).

decisions.choice: wiped out: erased, as writing is wiped from a page
decisions.reason: Psalm 51:3, 51:11 and Isaiah 43:25 speak of God blotting out sins.

decisions.choice: times of refreshing: seasons of relief and rest that God gives
alternatives: only a time at the end
decisions.reason: The word means a breathing space, relief. It may be the blessing that comes now to those who repent, or the age to come when Jesus returns; the sentence goes on to his coming.

decisions.choice: appointed beforehand: chosen in advance
decisions.reason: God chose Jesus beforehand to be the Messiah for Israel.

decisions.choice: heaven must receive him: Jesus stays in heaven until then
decisions.reason: The grammar allows either, but Jesus has been taken up into heaven (1:11), where he remains until he comes again.

decisions.choice: the restoration of all things: God setting everything right
alternatives: the return of every person to God
decisions.reason: The word is related to "restore" in 1:6. The prophets spoke of God renewing his people and his world (Isaiah 65:17; Malachi 4:6).

decisions.choice: turn away from your sins and come back to God
decisions.reason: Readable says what both verbs mean together.

decisions.choice: Jesus must be welcomed into heaven (B); Jesus must stay in heaven (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus and keep him as the subject.

source.text: Μωϋσῆς μὲν εἶπεν ὅτι Προφήτην ὑμῖν ἀναστήσει κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἐκ τῶν ἀδελφῶν ὑμῶν ὡς ἐμέ· αὐτοῦ ἀκούσεσθε κατὰ πάντα ὅσα ἂν λαλήσῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: Moses indeed said, A prophet for you will raise up Lord the God of you from the brothers of you like me; him you will listen to in all things whatever he may speak to you.

en.L: Moses said, 'A prophet [the] Lord your God will raise up for you from your brothers, like me. You shall listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in all things, whatever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may say to you.
en.B: Moses himself said, 'From among your own people the Lord your God will raise up a prophet for you, one like me. Whatever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to you, you must heed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in all of it.
en.R: Moses said, 'The Lord your God will give you a prophet like me. He will come from your own people. You must listen to everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} tells you.

fr.L: Moïse a dit : “Un prophète, le Seigneur votre Dieu vous [le] suscitera d’entre vos frères, comme moi. Lui, vous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}écouterez en tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous dira.
fr.B: Moïse lui-même a dit : “Du milieu de votre propre peuple, le Seigneur votre Dieu fera se lever pour vous un prophète semblable à moi. Quoi qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous dise, écoutez-{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} en tout.
fr.R: Moïse a dit : “Le Seigneur votre Dieu vous donnera un prophète comme moi. Il viendra de votre propre peuple. Vous devrez écouter tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous dira.

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 18:15-19: the prophet like Moses
decisions.reason: Moses promised that God would raise up a prophet like him. Peter quotes the Greek Old Testament freely and runs on into 3:23.

decisions.choice: the prophet like Moses is Jesus
decisions.reason: Stephen applies the same words to Jesus (7:37). At the transfiguration the voice says, "Listen to him" (Luke 9:35).

decisions.choice: will raise up: bring onto the scene
decisions.reason: In Deuteronomy the verb means to bring a prophet forward. Peter may hear the resurrection in it too (3:26).

decisions.choice: your brothers: your own people, Israel
decisions.reason: The prophet would be an Israelite.

decisions.choice: your own people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "brothers" means here; Literal keeps it.

source.text: ἔσται δὲ πᾶσα ψυχὴ ἥτις ἂν μὴ ἀκούσῃ τοῦ προφήτου ἐκείνου ἐξολεθρευθήσεται ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: It will be now every soul who not listens to the prophet that will be utterly destroyed from the people.

en.L: And it will be [that] every soul that does not listen to that prophet will be utterly destroyed from among the people.'
en.B: Every person who refuses to heed that prophet will be destroyed and removed from the people.'
en.R: Anyone who does not listen to that prophet will be destroyed and will no longer belong to God's people.'

fr.L: Et il arrivera [que] toute âme qui n’écoutera pas ce prophète sera exterminée du milieu du peuple.”
fr.B: Toute personne qui refusera d’écouter ce prophète sera détruite et retranchée du peuple.”
fr.R: Celui qui n’écoutera pas ce prophète sera détruit et ne fera plus partie du peuple de Dieu.”

decisions.choice: utterly destroyed from the people: the words of Leviticus 23:29
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 18:19 says God will call to account anyone who will not listen. Peter takes the stronger words from Leviticus 23:29, where they are spoken of anyone who does not humble himself on the Day of Atonement.

decisions.choice: every soul: every person
decisions.reason: As at 2:41.

decisions.choice: will no longer belong to God's people
decisions.reason: Readable says what being destroyed "from the people" means.

source.text: καὶ πάντες δὲ οἱ προφῆται ἀπὸ Σαμουὴλ καὶ τῶν καθεξῆς ὅσοι ἐλάλησαν καὶ κατήγγειλαν τὰς ἡμέρας ταύτας.

records.literal_gloss: And all now the prophets from Samuel and those following, as many as spoke, also announced the days these.

en.L: And also all the prophets from Samuel and those after [him], as many as have spoken, also announced these days.
en.B: And every prophet who has spoken, from Samuel on through those who followed him, has also told of these days.
en.R: Samuel and all the other prophets after him spoke about what is happening now.

fr.L: Et aussi tous les prophètes depuis Samuel et ceux qui [l’]ont suivi, tous ceux qui ont parlé, ont aussi annoncé ces jours-ci.
fr.B: Et tous les prophètes qui ont parlé, depuis Samuel et ceux qui l’ont suivi, ont eux aussi annoncé ces jours.
fr.R: Samuel et tous les autres prophètes après lui ont parlé de ce qui arrive maintenant.

decisions.choice: Samuel: the first of the prophets after Moses
decisions.reason: Samuel was known as a prophet throughout Israel (1 Samuel 3:20; Acts 13:20). He anointed David, to whom God's promise was given (1 Samuel 16:13; 2 Samuel 7).

decisions.choice: these days: the time now begun with Jesus
decisions.reason: As Joel's "last days" have begun (2:17).

source.text: ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ υἱοὶ τῶν προφητῶν καὶ τῆς διαθήκης ἧς διέθετο ὁ θεὸς πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας ὑμῶν, λέγων πρὸς Ἀβραάμ Καὶ ἐν τῷ σπέρματί σου ἐνευλογηθήσονται πᾶσαι αἱ πατριαὶ τῆς γῆς.

records.literal_gloss: You are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant which made the God with the fathers of you, saying to Abraham, And in the seed of you will be blessed all the families of the earth.

en.L: You are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant that God made with your fathers, saying to Abraham, 'And in your seed all the families of the earth will be blessed.'
en.B: You are the {{gender:children|sons}} of the prophets and of the covenant God made with your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to Abraham, 'All the families of the earth will be blessed through your offspring.'
en.R: You are the {{gender:children|sons}} of the prophets. The covenant God made with your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} belongs to you. God said to Abraham, 'Through your family all the families on earth will be blessed.'

fr.L: Vous êtes les fils des prophètes et de l’alliance que Dieu a conclue avec vos pères, en disant à Abraham : “Et en ta semence seront bénies toutes les familles de la terre.”
fr.B: Vous êtes les {{gender:enfants|fils}} des prophètes et de l’alliance que Dieu a conclue avec vos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}, quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a dit à Abraham : “Toutes les familles de la terre seront bénies par ta descendance.”
fr.R: Vous êtes les {{gender:enfants|fils}} des prophètes. L’alliance que Dieu a faite avec vos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} est pour vous. Dieu a dit à Abraham : “Par ta famille, toutes les familles de la terre seront bénies.”

decisions.choice: sons of the prophets and of the covenant: those to whom they belong
decisions.reason: "Sons of" here means heirs: the prophets spoke to them, and the covenant was made for them.

decisions.choice: God's promise to Abraham: Genesis 22:18, with 12:3
decisions.reason: Genesis 22:18 has "in your seed all the nations of the earth will be blessed"; Genesis 12:3 and 28:14 have "families".

decisions.choice: seed: offspring, Abraham's descendants, and Jesus as the one descendant
decisions.reason: The word is singular and can mean many descendants or one. 3:26 points to Jesus, through whom the blessing comes; Paul makes the point in Galatians 3:16.

decisions.choice: covenant: the binding promise God made
decisions.reason: God set the covenant and bound himself by it (Genesis 15, 17).

decisions.choice: children and ancestors, with "sons" and "fathers" as the alternatives
decisions.reason: The words mean the whole people, men and women; Literal keeps them.

decisions.choice: l’alliance at every level (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet settles: "l’alliance" is the French word for God's binding promise (m4); "le testament" now means a will, and "le pacte" sounds like a human treaty.

decisions.choice: ta semence (L); ta descendance (B); ta famille (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek picture of seed, singular, which leaves open the reading of one descendant (m3, uncertain); Balanced and Readable say what it means in current French.

source.text: ὑμῖν πρῶτον ἀναστήσας ὁ θεὸς τὸν παῖδα αὐτοῦ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτὸν εὐλογοῦντα ὑμᾶς ἐν τῷ ἀποστρέφειν ἕκαστον ἀπὸ τῶν πονηριῶν ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: To you first, having raised up the God the servant of him, sent him blessing you in the to turn away each from the wickednesses of you.

en.L: To you first God, having raised up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant, sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, blessing you in turning each [of you] away from your wicked deeds."
en.B: It was for you first that God raised up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant and sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to bless you, turning each one of you away from your evil deeds."
en.R: God raised up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Jesus and sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to you first. He sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to bless you by turning each of you away from the evil things you do."

fr.L: C’est à vous d’abord que Dieu, ayant suscité {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur, {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a envoyé vous bénir, en détournant chacun [de vous] de vos méchancetés. »
fr.B: C’est pour vous d’abord que Dieu a suscité {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur et {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a envoyé vous bénir, en détournant chacun de vous de ses mauvaises actions. »
fr.R: Dieu a fait se lever {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a envoyé d’abord vers vous. Il {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a envoyé pour vous bénir, en détournant chacun de vous du mal que vous faites. »

decisions.choice: raised up: brought forward as the promised prophet, and raised from the dead
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the prophet in 3:22, and of the resurrection in 2:24 and 2:32.

decisions.choice: to you first: to Israel first, and then to the nations
decisions.reason: The blessing promised to "all the families of the earth" (3:25) begins with Israel (13:46; Romans 1:16).

decisions.choice: in turning each of you away: Jesus turns them from evil
alternatives: as each of you turns away
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to turn someone else away or to turn oneself. The blessing is the turning itself.

decisions.choice: servant: as in 3:13
decisions.reason: The same word and the same title from Isaiah.

decisions.choice: his servant Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names him.
